items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: And then, Jimmy Harrison was trombone. And then I had a fellow in there called Fats. I don't know what Fats' name was. He was a friend of Jimmy's. ... So later on he went with Fats Waller.

ctx.x: But, what kind of music did you play? Of course, you played marches, but did you play anything else?

Oh yeah, Sousa marches, and then they started -- we tried to imitate, one thing that we tried to imitate was Jim Europe, at the Fifteenth, they had a fellow named Fats. And Fats played -- from Chicago -- and he played this "Bugle Blues." That's the first time I heard the Bugle Blues, and

so -- but I know some fellows later on have claimed that they originated the 'Bugle Blues', but they didn't. It was originated in the Army, in the Fifteenth Regiment. And, see, we tried to copy it from them because we had a chance to hear them once. We played it, we was the only outfit that played guard mount for the Marines. We was connected with the First Army Headquarters and the -- and we had some awful experiences over there because -- one of the experiences we had, the boys got kind of gay one time, so they…
